gates.acceptance: Every reused implementation, asset and data corpus has verified applicable permission at its pinned revision. Excluded NeTo/Spec implementations, schemas, descriptors and generated bindings remain unused; no access-denial workaround.
Independently establish rights for embedded sayings/calendar/seed/asset material or use approved original replacement data with an explicit behavior/content-change note.

Execute framework and gateway differential tests for service routes, aliases, constraints, binding defaults, trailing slash, percent encoding, methods/405 and content negotiation. Static attributes alone are insufficient.

Pin every exposed DTO and error shape, null/omission, dictionary casing, enum numbers, GUIDs, decimals, timestamps, content types, headers and validation/exception serialization from permitted evidence.

Recover global authentication/fallback policy, session/claim mapping, permission middleware and anonymous/unavailable behavior from eligible evidence. Synthetic bypasses stay explicit and production defaults deny.

Verify per-resource owner/member/admin/visibility permissions, revocation, role changes, dependency failures and request-scoped identity. No guessed permission strings, numeric roles or real credential issuance.

Pin licensed table/column/default/index/FK and soft-delete/audit behavior for every operation. Use actual disposable PostgreSQL tests for transactions, count/page consistency, isolation, concurrency and restart.

Define transport contracts only from permitted licensed callers or authorized documentation; prove cache/event envelopes, keying, protobuf interoperability, ordering, acknowledgment, retry, idempotency and websocket fanout. Unknown wire details remain blocked.
Validate synthetic object references, streaming, size limits, archive/media handling, quota and ACL behavior, failure cleanup, cancellation and recovery; no production buckets or files.

Test credential/signature state machines only with inert synthetic material. Production key/session/token creation, storage, rotation and revocation require verified policy and separately authorized integration.

Use controlled fixture providers until external API contracts, error handling, signatures, timeouts, idempotency and required account permissions are verified. No live payment, message, federation or account operation during migration tests.
Map every scheduler registration, hosted worker and listener; establish timezone/misfire, leases, cluster behavior, retry/ack, clock boundaries, duplicate execution, restart and catch-up semantics.
Verify defaults and required settings, secret loading, service names/discovery, URLs, ports, serializer settings and config-binding differences; never infer missing shared constants.
Prove synthetic data copy/reconciliation, migration up/down and rollback, dual-write/cutover ownership, connection loss, process crash/restart and bounded operator recovery.

Build actual services/containers; verify health/readiness, TLS, metrics/logs/traces, graceful shutdown, required native media libraries and exact-commit CI/client smoke before any production-ready claim.

phases.name: Establish the evidence ledger
phases.work: Freeze the permitted baseline and source hashes. Map HTTP actions, local RPC implementation methods, scheduler registrations and DbSets. Keep missing contracts and per-operation implementations as separate states; this plan provides the initial ledger.
phases.exit: 98 controller files reconcile to 818 static attributes; source integrity gate passes; no unsupported runtime-endpoint or production-completion claim.

phases.name: Finish bounded lawful runnable families
phases.work: Close runtime acceptance on recovered catalog/badge implementations and locally completed NodeInfo/miniapp package candidates. Do not expand candidate-only surface indefinitely while authority/schema/wire facts remain unresolved.
phases.exit: Each claimed operation has a source-backed synthetic fixture, HTTP error/binding checks, actual process smoke, relevant persistence/restart result and a precise production-gap statement.

phases.name: Implement local domain and persistence
phases.work: Parallelize Develop project/product/board rules, Passport notable-day/realm/progression rules, Sphere taxonomy/post/feed selection, Messager message/room transactions and Wallet ledger/order/subscription state machines. Do not wait on auth to write isolated domain/repository tests.
phases.exit: Per-family success/failure/concurrency tests exercise real disposable PostgreSQL; no in-memory substitute is counted as persistence; full exposed shared models remain gated until legally established.

phases.name: Resolve authority and shared contracts
phases.work: Use independently permitted interface evidence or rights-holder-approved specifications for missing claims, permission strings, shared model serialization, enums and wire descriptors. Keep unavailable facts explicit; do not import excluded sources or guess values.
phases.exit: Authenticated and anonymous differential tests, permission denial matrix and interoperable transport fixtures pass without excluded artifacts.

phases.name: Connect events, jobs, storage and providers
phases.work: Wire tested local domains to cache/NATS/websocket/RPC adapters, object-store/media pipelines and controlled provider fixtures. Cover registered jobs and hosted workers, not just HTTP methods.
phases.exit: Integration tests prove replay/idempotency, retry/ack, multi-replica coordination, storage cleanup and crash/restart behavior; no live provider side effect was required.

phases.name: Verify full services and clients
phases.work: Reconcile the action ledger with executable ASP.NET/gateway discovery and complete authorized client scenarios across existing Go identity/gateway/storage/notification services.
phases.exit: Every in-scope operation is matched to an implementation, passing evidence or an explicit agreed omission; route/model/authority/event/storage parity is validated end to end.

phases.name: Rehearse migration and release
phases.work: Build containers and run synthetic data migration/reconciliation, rollback, failure recovery, configuration/health/readiness and load tests before a separately authorized cutover.
phases.exit: Exact published commit has passing required CI, artifact/source manifests and a tested rollback plan. No production-complete claim while any required gate remains pending.

acceptance: A completed operation has an exact implementation path, permitted source/contract evidence and reproducible passing tests for its success and failure cases; a static route record is never counted as completion.
A completed family includes repository/domain behavior, authority, serialization, errors, persistence, jobs/events/storage/provider interactions and restart/recovery appropriate to that family.
Any synthetic-only candidate remains disabled or fail-closed by default for production use, with explicit fake principal/status/schema configuration and no in-memory fallback presented as PostgreSQL.
No generated descriptor or binding, protocol schema, shared implementation or missing-license data corpus is used as a shortcut for unknown contracts.
No actual payment, credential issuance, production write, external notification, live federation or provider action is necessary for acceptance fixtures.
Unit, race, contract, source-integrity, actual-PostgreSQL and process-smoke evidence is recorded distinctly. Skipped, failed and never-run checks are not reported as passing.
Full completion requires a reconciled runtime operation ledger, all required release gates, existing-Go service/client integration, exact-commit CI and a synthetic migration/rollback rehearsal.
